definition_of_done: Running `printf 'a b\n' | wordcount -` prints exactly `words: 2 characters: 2 lines: 1` followed by a newline to stdout, prints nothing to stderr, and exits with status 0.
Running `wordcount -` with empty standard input prints exactly `words: 0 characters: 0 lines: 0` followed by a newline to stdout and exits with status 0.

Running `wordcount -` with the bytes b'\xff\xfe' on standard input prints exactly one stderr line `wordcount: error: file is not valid UTF-8 text: <stdin>`, prints nothing to stdout, writes no traceback, and exits with status 1.

For each byte sample b'a b
', b'a
b
', b'ab' and 'café naïve 日本
' encoded as UTF-8, `wordcount PATH` on a file holding the sample and `wordcount -` fed the sample on stdin print identical stdout lines.
Running `wordcount - extra` prints argparse usage to stderr, prints nothing to stdout, and exits with status 2.
README.md documents the `wordcount -` invocation, states that `-` reads standard input until end of input, and documents `wordcount ./-` for a file literally named `-`.
regression_guardrails: Invoking `wordcount` with no argument still prints argparse usage to stderr and exits with status 2, and it does not read standard input.
A file literally named `-` is still counted through `wordcount ./-` with the unchanged three-field output line.
The existing SPEC-0001 to SPEC-0003 tests pass unchanged: no existing test function in tests/ is modified or removed, and `uv run pytest` exits 0.

SPEC.feature_name: Standard input through an explicit '-' argument
SPEC.context:
Users want to count text piped into wordcount without writing a temporary file. Today `cat notes.txt | wordcount -` treats '-' as a path and fails with `file not found: -`. This gap was deferred across three strategies and DG-0004 names it as the core pipeline need.

STRAT-0004 commits to an explicit '-' argument whose text flows through the same single decode and counting path as a file. Counts, the output line and error contracts stay identical across sources. Only error messages name `<stdin>` instead of a path. No argument stays a usage error with exit status 2, and stdin is never read implicitly.
api_contracts: Console command `wordcount PATH | -`: exactly one positional argument, parsed by argparse in hello.cli.main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int.
`wordcount -` reads all bytes from sys.stdin.buffer until end of input.
`wordcount PATH` reads the file bytes as before.
Both sources pass their bytes to one shared UTF-8 decode step in src/hello/cli.py with no newline translation.
Success output for both sources: exactly one stdout line `words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>` (ADR-0008).
Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: one stderr line `wordcount: error: file is not valid UTF-8 text: <stdin>`, empty stdout, exit status 1 (ADR-0004).
Zero arguments, or more than one argument including `-` plus another: argparse usage on stderr, exit status 2.
data_models: No new data model. The decoded text is a plain str passed unchanged to count_words, count_characters and count_lines.
The source name used in error messages is the PATH string for files and the literal `<stdin>` for '-'.
dependencies: Architecture ARCH-0001 v1.2 update that moves stdin processing and the '-' argument out of the hello and hello-cli 'Does NOT own' lists.
The four AGENTS.md Quality Gate commands (ADR-0003)
constraints: Counting logic stays in the pure counters; stdin handling lives only in hello.cli (ADR-0002).
Stdin is decoded once, through the same decode step as files, never through sys.stdin's text layer.
Stdin is read only when the argument is exactly '-'.
File-path error messages and exit statuses are unchanged.

decisions.text: We will treat the single argument '-' as standard input, read it as raw bytes from sys.stdin.buffer, and decode it through the same UTF-8 decode step used for files, naming the source `<stdin>` in error messages.
decisions.title: Explicit '-' stdin marker sharing the file decode path
decisions.context: Users need to count piped text. The architecture forbids a second decoding path or newline translation, and no argument must stay a usage error with exit status 2.
alternatives: Read stdin implicitly when no argument is given: rejected, it breaks the exit status 2 usage contract.
Auto-detect piped input: rejected, behavior depends on the calling environment and conflicts with the usage error.
Read stdin through sys.stdin text mode: rejected, universal-newline translation would change CR and CRLF line counts.
Copy stdin to a temporary file: rejected, it adds filesystem writes and error messages would name a temporary path.
positive_consequences: Counts are identical for identical bytes from either source.
Error contracts stay the same, with `<stdin>` in place of a path.
The convention matches common Unix tools.
negative_consequences: A file literally named '-' must be reached through './-'.
An interactive terminal on stdin waits for end of input, which can look like a hang.
The invalid UTF-8 message says `file` even for standard input.

enforcement.rule: hello.cli reads stdin only via sys.stdin.buffer when the argument is exactly '-', and decodes stdin and file bytes through one shared decode step with no newline translation.
enforcement.mechanism: Code review of src/hello/cli.py by the spec critic against this ADR

architecture_change.summary: Let wordcount read standard input through an explicit '-' argument, sharing the single decode and counting path with files (STRAT-0004).

changed.name: hello
changed.owns: Giving users local, dependency-free text utilities. It currently reports the word count, the non-whitespace character count and the terminated-line count of one input in a single invocation. The input is one text file or standard input.
changed.does_not_own: Other text statistics beyond word, character and line counts, such as bytes, longest line or per-line output. Several inputs in one invocation, totals, implicit or auto-detected stdin, non-UTF-8 encodings, or distribution through a public package index.
changed.deployment: Installed from the repository into a local Python environment on the user's machine.
changed.technology: Python (current stable release), standard library only

changed.name: hello command-line package
changed.owns: The installable src-layout hello package and its console command. The command takes one file path, or the '-' argument for standard input. It prints that input's word, character and line counts on one line and exits with a status code.
changed.does_not_own: Any network access, persistent state, configuration files, or third-party runtime dependencies. Command-line flags or arguments beyond the single PATH or '-' argument. Reading standard input when no argument is given.
changed.deployment: Run as a local process on the user's machine after installing the package from the repository into the project environment.
changed.technology: Python standard library; console entry point declared in pyproject.toml; environment managed with the existing lockfile tooling

changed.name: Word-count command
changed.owns: Parsing the single argument: a file path, or '-' for standard input. It reads the chosen source once and decodes it as UTF-8 along one shared path. It passes that same decoded text to the word, character and line counters. It prints the three counts as one line in the form `words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>`. It turns a missing file, an unreadable file or undecodable content into a one-line stderr message, a non-zero exit status and empty stdout. Messages for standard input name `<stdin>`, and file-path messages and statuses are unchanged.
changed.does_not_own: The definition of what a word, a visible character or a line is, or counting logic of any kind. It does not decode text a second time, along a separate path per source, or with newline translation. It does not read standard input when no argument is given. A file literally named '-' is reached only through './-'.

relations_added.description: Passes the decoded text from the file or standard input in an in-process function call and receives the integer word count.
Passes the decoded text from the file or standard input in an in-process function call and receives the integer visible-character count.
Passes the same decoded text given to the word and character counters, in an in-process function call, and receives the terminated-line count.
